result.strongest_objection: Option B's claimed semantic and concurrency safety rests on V5/V6, but those greps do not establish slice immutability. V25 proves `Elements` is exposed as a raw `[]Value`; a caller can alias it and execute `xs[i] = v`, which neither matches `.Elements[i] =` nor is prevented by three-index capacity clipping. An arena-backed prepend shares the old elements with the new list, so such a write can mutate both logical list versions or race with readers—behavior that copy-on-cons does not have.
result.catch: Capacity clipping prevents append from overwriting arena storage, but it does nothing against indexed writes through escaped aliases. The conflict-surface audit must cover transitive slice aliases and mutation-capable callees, not only direct `.Elements` assignments and `append(X.Elements, ...)` syntax.
result.proposed_fix: Make immutable ownership a prerequisite for Option B. Replace the V5/V6 safety claim with a verification row produced by Go AST/data-flow analysis that inventories every return, assignment, and function call through which `ListValue.Elements` can escape or be mutated. Change `SafeAsList` and every other externally mutable exposure to return a cloned, capacity-clipped slice, and add tests proving mutation of each returned slice cannot alter either the source list or a prepended descendant. Add an enforced analyzer/linter rule forbidding writes or mutation-capable escapes of arena-backed storage. If that invariant cannot be mechanically enforced without privatizing `Elements` and adding read-only accessors, reject Option B and redesign around an actually immutable representation.

result.strongest_objection: The design fails to bootstrap the arena chain for `std/list`'s `[x] ++ rest` pattern. The recursion base cases (`[]` or literals) have a nil arena by definition. If `concat_List` only attempts a fast-path claim and defaults to the legacy copy path when the right operand lacks sufficient slack, it will return a new list with a nil arena. This nil arena will propagate up the entire recursive call stack, causing every subsequent `++` to miss the fast path and keeping `std/list` exactly as O(n²) as it is today.
result.catch: `concat_List`'s small-left path is missing an arena-allocating slow path to handle nil-arena right operands.
result.proposed_fix: Update the `concat_List` section to explicitly state that if the right operand lacks sufficient slack (e.g., nil arena), the small-left path must allocate a fresh arena with geometric front slack, mirroring `Prepend`'s slow path. Alternatively, mandate that `concat_List` delegates directly to `Prepend` when `len(left) == 1`.
